reasoning_traces.think:
The recipe encodes a constrained optimization problem where cost C is minimized subject to serving size S and flavor profile F. The spice intensity model defines a parametric function I(n,t) that maps chili count and simmer time to perceived heat level. The marinade dynamics describe how flavor penetrates chicken over time, modeled by a diffusion-like process. These primitives form a dual system: one optimizing economic constraints (cost), the other optimizing sensory outcomes (flavor). Failure modes include over-simmering leading to bitter taste, under-marinating causing uneven flavor, and poor substitution choices increasing cost beyond target. The system exhibits nonlinearity in flavor perception due to capsaicin concentration and synergistic effects of multiple spices.
